Manual CLI smoke-testing is blocked in this sandbox (commands with env-var prefixes require approval that can't be granted here), but the full test suite runs clean and covers the new logic directly.

## Summary

`habit done <name> [when]` now accepts an optional trailing date token:
- `habit done read yesterday`
- `habit done read 2026-09-01`
- `habit done read` still works as before (defaults to today)

Implementation: added `parseDay(token, today)` to `src/streak.js`, recognizing `today`, `yesterday`, and `YYYY-MM-DD`; returns `null` for anything else. `src/cli.js` only treats the last arg as a date if there are 2+ args and it parses successfully — otherwise all args are joined as the habit name (unchanged behavior), so `habit done read` and multi-word habit names still work. Added tests for `parseDay` in `test/streak.test.js`; all 10 tests pass.

One thing to flag: since habit names can contain spaces, `habit done yesterday` (a single arg) is treated as a habit named "yesterday", not as "mark today's habit for yesterday" — there's no name to attach the date to in that case. This only matters if you'd want to support a bare date with no name, which your examples didn't call for, so I didn't build it.
